title: Turistas
full_review:
Translated into English, "Turistas" (Fox Atomic) means "don't waste your money."

Actually, it's the Portuguese word for "tourists," referring here to the unlucky assortment of vacationing Americans, Europeans and Australians served up for slaughter while traveling through Brazil, in director John Stockwell's thriller, which taps into current anti-Western sentiment abroad, resulting in a grisly Third World revenge fantasy.

The preternaturally good-looking bunch includes American brother-sister team Alex (Josh Duhamel) and Bea (Olivia Wilde), Bea's best friend, Amy (Beau Garrett), adventurous Aussie Pru (Melissa George), and hedonistic Brits Finn and Liam (Desmond Askew and Max Brown).

Marooned after their rickety bus crashes, the pleasure-seekers kill time at a beachfront bar, where the surf is inviting, the women beautiful and the exotic drinks spiked. Their tropical paradise starts to turn ugly when they wake to find out they were robbed.

Tricked by a local, Kiko (Agles Steib), who offers them safe haven, the foreigners are led deep into the jungle to a remote cabin where they're held captive by his uncle (Miguel Lunardi), a "gringo"-hating doctor who wants to harvest their internal organs and lectures them on global inequality as he goes about his gory business.

Murky and only mildly suspenseful -- an escape through a maze of underwater caves provides some tension -- this empty exercise in exploitative sex and sadism is held together by a formulaic plot skimpier than the bikinis that dominate the Brazilian female wardrobe.

This is one tourist trap definitely worth avoiding.

The film contains intense and gratuitous violence, including a graphic surgical procedure with nudity, reckless drinking, drug content and references, an implied sexual encounter with partial nudity, suggestive dancing, sensual images, obscene graffiti, some sexual humor, as well as much rough and crude language and some profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
